author: Wes Adams
title: Big Upgrades Coming to GJ Airport - NewsBreak
text:
By Wes Adams ,
2 hours ago
For the last couple of years, it seems like any time there was good news about an airport in Western Colorado , the news was about Montrose . Now it’s time for Grand Junction to enjoy a little excitement following big news in August about a new FAA grant awarded to Grand Junction’s Regional Airport.
Find out why the city is hopeful that the grant will not only help our community keep growing, but that it will also help aid Mesa County’s wildfire response.
AA Grant Boosts Grand Junction Regional Airport Wirestock An FAA grant of $12.5 million sounds like a big win, but that is only part of the good news here. According to The Business Times , Grand Junction has secured more than $150 million in grants since 2018. This is funding that will help several airport projects move forward, including the runway sub-base. Stacking up grants allows for more leverage with the FAA’s 95% funding match , which means upgrades for Grand Junction taxpayers who did not have to fund nearly as much of the project.
$200M Capital Program Brings Major Upgrades Google Street The extra funds will help make several changes happen at Grand Junction Regional Airport, starting with the relocation of Runway 11/29 . A portion of the current runway will be converted into a taxiway, and the new runway will be the centerpiece of the airport. Pavement rehab, new gates, and expanded parking will also be part of the upgrades thanks to the $200 million Capital Improvement Program . The new runway is expected to open in 2029.
Wildfire Hub and Future Terminal Plans The Bureau of Land Management has invested $9 million to build a multi-use aviation facility at the airport as a hub for wildfire response. The facility would support firefighters, dispatchers, engineers, and fuel techs during wildfire season. A new runway means larger tankers could assist firefighters in a big way in just a few years.
Terminal expansion remains in the early planning stage, with designs and costs still being finalized. While details remain limited, the plan calls for more space and modern amenities, with construction expected to begin around 2026 or 2027, according to Wikipedia.

Keep reading to check out seventeen reminders about items you should not place in your suitcase before heading to Denver International Airport. Gallery Credit: Wesley Adams Canva pro 17 Items Banned from Checked Bags at Denver’s Airport The following items must be carried on the plane with you or left at home when flying out of Denver International Airport. Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Alcohol 140 Proff Strong alcohol over 140 proof is not allowed to fly in a checked bag OR a carry-on. You’ll have to leave the good stuff at home.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Bear Spray Bear Spray for the hiking trail is too dangerous to carry on or to pack in a checked bag. Do not attempt to travel with this or it will likely be missing from your bag when you get to your destination.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Cordless Curling Iron Since these come with a lithium battery or a butane cartridge, they are not allowed in a checked bag. Carry-on usually requires a safety cover for the heating element and protection from accidental activation.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Non-Stick Cooking Spray You’ll need to go and purchase some non-stick cooking spray when you reach your destination. It is not allowed on the plane inside checked bags or a carry-on in Denver.
Getty Images photo-by-eamonn-m-mccormack Items Banned From Checked Bags: English Christmas Crackers These special crackers come in a cardboard tube with a chemically treated paper strip inside that pops and causes a puff of smoke when you open the tube. It makes sense why these do not belong on a plane, right?
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Live Fish You can fly with a live lobster in a checked bag but not a live fish. Go figure.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Live Coral Live Coral, like live fish, are not allowed in checked bags at the Denver airport.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Personal Oxygen Bottle Personal oxygen bottles are not permitted in checked bags at Denver airport.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Power Banks Like to charge your devices at the airport? No problem, you’ll just need to carry on these lithium-ion batteries. Do not check them.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Samsung Galaxy Note 7 A serious battery defect keeps this phone on a list of electronics you cannot bring on a plane. It’s been banned since 2016.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Spray Starch That freshly ironed look will have to wait till you arrive at your destination because spray starch is not allowed on planes as a checked item or a carry-on item.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Bang Snaps Traveling for the 4th of July? Leave the bang snaps at home. They are not allowed as a checked item or in your carry-on bag.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Dynamite The TSA may never let you fly again if they find this in your checked bag or your carry-on. Do not bring dynamite to the airport.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Replicas of Explosives Have you got a souvenir replica grenade from the set of RAMBO? Leave it at home. Replicas of explosives are not allowed in checked or carry-on bags.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: E-Cigarettes/ Vaping Devices These items also can contain lithium-ion batteries and are not allowed in your checked bag. Some can be carried on the plan depending on the battery size but none can be in a checked bag.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Lighter Fluid I know you want to fire up the grill as soon as you arrive, but you can take the lighter fluid on the plane as a carry-on or checked item.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Safety Matches You cannot place safety matches in a checked bag. You can carry a single book of them in your carry-on if you need to.
Canva Pro Items Banned From Checked Bags: Party Poppers Because of the powder inside party poppers, they are not allowed on plans as checked items or with your carry-on.
